title: Crüger to Müller, Easter Monday 1620
author: Peter Crüger
source: Peter Crüger's letter to Philipp Müller of Easter Monday 1620, written at Danzig after he had received Kepler's three books on comets (Augsburg, 1619). He rejects Kepler's straight-line paths for comets, because they assume the earth's annual motion, and finds the *Astronomia nova* and the *Harmonice mundi* hard going. The original is in the Bibliothèque de l'Observatoire, Paris (B, 1, 9; 89, 9. B. 24). Printed in extracts in *Nova Kepleriana* 4, ed. Walther von Dyck and Max Caspar, Abhandlungen der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Math.-naturw. Abteilung 31, no. 1 (Munich, 1927), 106–107.
transcribed_from: the page images of the 1927 printing.
summary: Crüger rejects Kepler's theory of straight-line comet paths because it assumes the earth's annual motion, mocks the 'rabid leaps' it implies, and finds the *Astronomia nova* and *Harmonice mundi* hard to follow.

notes.on: a friend to you above all your friends
notes.note: An echo of the proverb *amicus Plato, sed magis amica veritas*: Plato is a friend, but truth a greater one.
